title: Wisconsin: history overview

definition: Wisconsin: the Badger State, admitted 1848 (30th); capital Madison.
description: Wisconsin — "Badger State" — entered the Union 1848 (30th). Its capital is Madison and its largest city is Milwaukee. Ho-Chunk; lead mining. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Wisconsin achieved statehood 1848 (30th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Dairy state; progressivism. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Wisconsin its number among the states.

Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Wisconsin's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Madison
d: Madison is the capital of Wisconsin.
definition: Madison is the capital of Wisconsin.
description: Madison has been the seat of Wisconsin government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Wisconsin's largest is Milwaukee — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Badger State
description: The nickname "Badger State" captures how Wisconsin sees itself — and how America sees it. Dairy made it America's Dairyland. title: Motto: Forward
d: The state motto of Wisconsin is "Forward."
